title: Pricing escalation & SSO approval handoff
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Northbridge through outstanding MSA redlines, DPA encryption wording, SSO/SAML integration plan, and pricing escalation path for reserved capacity. Agreed to follow up with redlined MSA, SSO runbook, and formal pricing approval package. Action items and ownership captured at the end.
topics: MSA redlines and audit log language
DPA encryption and data residency clauses
Dedicated pricing escalation and approval workflow
Onboarding timeline and pilot acceptance criteria
next_steps: Alex to send redlined MSA PDF highlighting section 6.2 (audit logs) by 2025-06-09
Priya to attach SSO integration runbook + SAML metadata by 2025-06-06
Ben to compile pricing approval packet (TCO worksheet + committed capacity terms) and share with Evelyn by 2025-06-10
Customer to confirm procurement gate date and decision forum by 2025-06-12
action_items: Owner: Alex Kim; Item: Prepare redline MSA with proposed audit log clause and DPA cross-reference; Due: 2025-06-09
Owner: Priya Rao; Item: Provide SAML metadata sample, SSO test plan, and list of IP ranges for allowlist; Due: 2025-06-06
Owner: Ben Torres; Item: Build pricing approval packet including annual committed capacity pricing, break-fix SLA targets, and fallback hosted pricing; Due: 2025-06-10
Owner: Daniel Ho (Customer); Item: Share internal sec review timeline and required encryption certs (KMS/HSM) list; Due: 2025-06-12
transcript: 00:00 Alex Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I see we have the Northbridge core group, appreciate you making time.
00:06 Marcus Lee: Yeah thanks Alex. We just wanted to run through the remaining MSA open items and the pricing escalation path before we kick off procurement — super time-sensitive for us.
00:14 Priya Rao: Cool, I'll do a quick SE overview of SSO and network requirements and then we can hit the MSA redlines. I have the latest redline open.
00:22 Sonia Patel: To be clear, Legal is focused on two things: auditability clause 6.2 and the DPA subprocessor list — we need definitive language not a best-efforts statement.
00:31 Alex Kim: Understood. In our last pass we added a standalone audit logs addendum. We can reframe into the MSA if that helps procurement's template.
00:39 Evelyn Ruiz: Procurement asks that any addendum be part of the MSA bundle so it flows into the SOW and PO. Otherwise legal flags it as a separate contract.
00:48 Daniel Ho: From a security standpoint we also need to confirm KMS usage and key custody — are customer-managed keys supported in the private deployment?

00:56 Priya Rao: Yes, for Redwood Private we support bringing your own KMS; we typically integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and enterprise HSMs. There was a little nuance with on-prem HSM cert provisioning but we have a playbook.

01:08 Marcus Lee: Great. For the DPA, can you confirm data residency controls? Northbridge requires EU residency for EU customers and US residency for US customers — is that possible with a hybrid routing policy?
01:16 Alex Kim: Yep, our routing supports region pinning. You can configure policies to route EU requests to EU-only instances; that's part of the Dedicated offering.

01:24 Sonia Patel: Back to the MSA: the audit logs clause as redlined references redwood-console logs retention; we need explicit retention windows and the ability to export logs into our SIEM for a minimum of 7 years — is that supported?

01:34 Priya Rao: Exporting to SIEM is supported via S3 push or syslog; retention of seven years is long but doable if you opt into extended log archival on Dedicated. We'll need to account for storage costs in the pricing packet.

01:45 Evelyn Ruiz: Which brings us to pricing escalation. Our finance team requires a committed capacity price that includes a clear escalation ladder if we increase GPU hours by more than 30% quarter-over-quarter.

01:54 Ben Torres: For committed capacity we have tiered pricing and a formal escalation policy — we can add a clause that defines thresholds, notice periods, and blended rates for overage. I'll include a worked example in the packet.
02:03 Marcus Lee: Important: any escalation must route through our procurement approval board; we need a one-page summary that procurement can sign off quickly.
02:11 Alex Kim: Noted. We'll prepare a one-pager with the escalation triggers, pricing table, and decision path. Ben will lead that.
02:18 Daniel Ho: About SSO — we run enterprise SAML with SCIM provisioning through Okta. We need a staged test plan and a sandbox service account. How long does setup typically take?

02:26 Priya Rao: Typical SSO + SCIM setup on Dedicated takes 3-5 business days for the initial handshake, then 1-2 days to validate group mappings. We'll provide metadata and a test identity provider config so your identity team can do an in-house smoke test.

02:35 Sonia Patel: Can you also confirm session timeout defaults and whether session tokens are encrypted at rest? We require session tokens to be encrypted with customer-managed keys for certain admin roles.
02:44 Priya Rao: Session tokens are stored server-side and we can encrypt session state at rest using the same KMS integration. We'll note role-based controls in the SAML mapping doc.

02:53 Marcus Lee: On the procurement side, we need to confirm the SLAs. Are you offering a credit-based SLA for Dedicated? We need uptime, P99 tail latency guarantees for inference endpoints, and an incident response timeline.

03:03 Ben Torres: For Dedicated we typically commit to 99.9% uptime and P99 inference latency targets that vary by model family and sequence length. For contractual SLA we can put response time SLOs: 30 minutes for Sev 1 initial response, 4 hours for remediation plan, etc.
03:14 Sonia Patel: We'll want definitions for Sev 1/2/3 in the contract. Also, what's the escalation path — who at Redwood gets looped in for exec-level issues?
03:22 Alex Kim: We'll include an escalation matrix — typically AE -> CSM -> Engineering manager -> VP of Ops. We can put names and pager contacts in the SLA appendix for the enterprise signature.
03:31 Evelyn Ruiz: On billing: procurement wants net-60, a PO referencing the SOW, and a single invoice per month. Any constraints?
03:38 Ben Torres: We can do net-60 with an enterprise billing term, and consolidate invoices. For committed capacity contracts we require a minimum annual commitment for the discounted rates.
03:46 Marcus Lee: What about termination liability? There was pushback in the last round about open-ended liability tied to model outputs; we want a carveout for downstream use cases.

03:55 Sonia Patel: Right, indemnity for model outputs — we need language that limits Redwood's liability for customer generated content, and clarifies Redwood will not be liable for regulatory fines from customer's misuse.
04:04 Alex Kim: We typically include a use-case limitation and mutual indemnification for IP. If needed we can carve out certain high-risk workloads into a separate SOW with tighter controls.
04:13 Daniel Ho: A couple of technical asks — can we get a shortlist of subprocessors and a SOC2 report? Also, any third-party cloud providers used in the EU routing?
04:21 Priya Rao: Yes, we publish a subprocessors list. We'll send the latest SOC 2 Type II and a summary of cloud regions and providers involved in EU tenancy.

04:30 Sonia Patel: For the DPA, our legal ops insists on termination data return: encrypted backups to a customer-provided S3 and proof of secure deletion from Redwood infrastructure. Can you meet that?
04:39 Priya Rao: We support encrypted backup exports; we can schedule a data export and provide deletion certificates. The process is documented in our private deployment runbook.
04:48 Marcus Lee: Let's talk timeline: Procurement has a gate meeting on 2025-06-18. We need all legal redlines, pricing packet, and SOC docs by 2025-06-12 to make that meeting.
04:56 Alex Kim: Ok that gives us ten days. We'll prioritize the MSA redline and the pricing packet. Can we commit to those dates now?
05:03 Evelyn Ruiz: Yes, if we have the one-pager and procurement packet by the 10th, procurement can prep the gate. Legal will still want a few days to review but that's within our window.
05:11 Ben Torres: I'll target 2025-06-10 for the packet and include an appendix with cost assumptions for archival logs and extended retention.
05:19 Priya Rao: I'll circulate a SSO checklist and the SAML metadata by 2025-06-06; that will let Daniel do the sandbox tests while legal finishes the MSA.

05:28 Sonia Patel: One other outstanding — audit rights. We need to be able to conduct an annual audit, or at minimum get an audit report from Redwood or your subprocessor. Can you confirm frequency and ownership?

05:37 Alex Kim: We allow customer audits on Dedicated with notice; alternatively we provide the SOC 2 and a limited audit rights schedule. We'll propose a clause that allows an annual third-party audit with reasonable notice and scoping.
05:46 Marcus Lee: Good. Compatibility question: if we start with Hosted to speed initial integration, can we move to Dedicated mid-contract without breaking pricing or SSO configs?

05:55 Priya Rao: You can absolutely migrate from Hosted to Dedicated. The SSO configs are reusable; network allowlist and private endpoints need to be updated but we support a migration plan. Pricing would be reconciled at cutover — we'll include a migration credit clause in the packet.
06:04 Sonia Patel: About exportability of logs: we may need a continuous ETL into our lake for regulatory archiving. Does Redwood support continuous push or is it batch only?

06:12 Priya Rao: We support both continuous streaming to SIEM and batch S3 exports. For high-volume telemetry we recommend streaming; we'll include bandwidth and storage notes in the pricing appendix.
06:21 Daniel Ho: Are there any known blockers around IP whitelisting? We operate strict egress rules at the corporate perimeter.
06:28 Priya Rao: We provide a static set of egress IPs for Dedicated and can support customer VPN/IPsec tunnels. We'll include the IP list with the SSO runbook.
06:36 Alex Kim: Quick check — Sonia, Marcus, is there any redline item beyond the audit logs, the indemnity, and the termination data return that would block procurement gating on the 18th?
06:44 Sonia Patel: Those are the main items. We may have minor language tweaks around SLA credits but nothing substantive that would block the gate if addressed by the 12th.
06:52 Marcus Lee: Okay, then the ask is clear. Also, Finance flagged we may need a signature authority clause for renewals — we will send the contact details for our approver.
07:00 Ben Torres: I'll add a renewal authority section to the procurement packet template so procurement has the fields they need.
07:08 Alex Kim: Great. We'll summarize action items now and confirm ownership.

07:12 Alex Kim: Alex — send redlined MSA with audit clause; Priya — SSO metadata and test plan; Ben — pricing packet and TCO worksheet. Customer will confirm procurement gate details and internal reviewer names.
07:22 Sonia Patel: Also please include the subprocessors list and the SOC2 PDF in that email thread; legal needs those documents to proceed with the DPA crosswalk.
07:29 Priya Rao: Will do, I'll attach SOC2 and subprocessors and call out the EU region provider list.
07:36 Daniel Ho: One small note — for the smoke test we'd like sample test vectors highlighting latency targets; can Redwood provide a small benchmark harness for our cloud team?
07:44 Priya Rao: Yes, we can provide a small benchmark harness and sample prompts. It will show p50/p95/p99 for the model family you're evaluating.
07:52 Marcus Lee: Excellent. Any other blockers?
07:55 Evelyn Ruiz: None from procurement. We'll wait for the packet. Thank you everyone.

07:59 Alex Kim: Thanks all. We'll follow up with a single email containing the redline, SSO docs, pricing packet, SOC2, and subprocessors list. Expect that by 2025-06-09 for the MSA redline and 2025-06-10 for the pricing packet.
08:11 [Meeting closes — informal chatter and calendar scheduling]
08:20 Ben Torres: (off mic) I'll also create a short one-page for the procurement gate as requested.
08:24 Alex Kim: Thanks Ben. We'll reconvene if any urgent items surface; otherwise follow-ups via email and a 30-minute check-in the week after the procurement gate if needed.
08:33 Marcus Lee: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
08:36 [End of recording]
